items.title: Showers4Less Expands Its Online Shower Catalog Past 400 Products and Opens Applications for Dealers and Installers
items.summary: Showers4Less refreshed its online catalog to more than 400 shower products, including ANZZI, and is now taking applications from dealers and installers.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 11, 2026 — Showers4Less, the online shower store at showers4less.com, has refreshed its catalog to more than 400 shower products and is now accepting applications from contractors who want to become Showers4Less dealers or installers. The refresh ran from September 25 to 27, 2026, and added a line of ANZZI shower products.

The store runs on Shopify, and Shop Pay checkout is active. Showers4Less belongs to the same family of companies as Aging Safely Baths, the Denver-area walk-in tub and accessible shower company. Quote requests on the USABusinessSearch.com directory are labeled "Aging Safely Baths / Showers4Less."

A dealer and installer program, open to applications

Contractors can apply through the contact form on showers4less.com by choosing the "Showers4Less Dealer Application" option. Applications are already coming in from contractors.

The program is meant for remodelers, plumbers, accessibility contractors and installers who already quote bathroom projects and want one online catalog to specify from. A contractor can send a homeowner to a product page, confirm the configuration together and check out on the same site, instead of trading spec sheets between suppliers.

"A good installer shouldn't have to hunt across a handful of suppliers to find the size and configuration a client needs. A bigger catalog and a real dealer program put more of that in one place. If you install showers for a living, apply, tell us where you work and we'll get back to you," the company said in a statement.

What changed in the catalog

  • A refreshed main catalog, updated September 25–27, 2026
  • ANZZI shower products, added September 26, 2026
  • Together, more than 400 shower products in one Shopify storefront
  • Shop Pay checkout available on the store

Why it matters for homeowners

Homeowners replacing a tub or upgrading to a walk-in shower often hit the same wall: the contractor they trust doesn't stock the product, and the product they like isn't sold by anyone nearby. A larger online catalog with an installer network behind it lets the two sides meet in the middle. A homeowner can browse first and bring a short list to the contractor, or a contractor can start from the catalog and send a link.

Shoppers who aren't sure what fits can email the sales team with the room dimensions and the product they're considering before they order.

How to apply or ask a question

Contractors can apply to become a dealer or installer, and shoppers can browse the full catalog, at www.showers4less.com. Product and dealer questions go to the sales team at 1-888-779-2284 or sales@showers4less.com.

About Showers4Less

Showers4Less is an online shower store at www.showers4less.com, built on Shopify, with a catalog of more than 400 shower products that includes ANZZI shower products. It sells to homeowners and works with contractors through a dealer and installer program. Showers4Less is part of the same family of companies as Aging Safely Baths.

items.title: Eye To Ad Media Opens Total Market Domination, Selling One Exclusive Industry Slot Per State on Its Business Directory Network
items.summary: One business per industry per state gets the pop-up and large banner placements on USABusinessSearch.com, plus COBusinessList.com for Colorado slots.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 11, 2026 — Denver-based Eye To Ad Media has opened Total Market Domination, an advertising package that sells one exclusive slot per industry in each state across the business directory network the company owns. When someone searches the network for an industry and a location in that state, such as "dentist Orlando" or "Omaha auto repair," the business holding the slot appears in a pop-up on the results, and its large banners sit on the matching search and category pages.

The network covers USABusinessSearch.com nationwide and adds COBusinessList.com for Colorado. While a business holds a slot, no competitor in its industry can buy the same slot in that state.

Why one slot per state

Exclusive directory sponsorships are often sold by a local newspaper or chamber of commerce, one town or one print edition at a time. Total Market Domination works at state level instead. That suits companies that serve a whole state or several metros in one: a roofer covering the Front Range, an HVAC company working across Arizona, or a personal injury firm that would rather claim a practice area statewide than fight for one city at a time.

We built this for owners who win on call volume and are tired of sharing every placement with every competitor in town. One business gets the slot for its industry in its state. We're also plain about what it isn't: it's advertising on directories we own, not Google, and nobody should promise you a number of calls.

Eye To Ad Media, in a company statement.

What is included

  • An exclusive slot for one industry in one state on the network
  • A pop-up placement on searches that match the industry and a location in that state
  • Large banner placements on matching search and category pages
  • The business name, phone number and website link on every placement
  • USABusinessSearch.com nationwide, with COBusinessList.com added for Colorado slots
  • Exact placements and terms confirmed in writing before the campaign starts

Pricing and limits

The normal rate is $2,500 per industry, per month, per state. Eye To Ad Media is offering lower launch rates while the network opens, and businesses can ask for current launch pricing in their market. Reach depends on how many people search the network for that industry in that state, and the company says it talks through what to expect before anyone commits. Total Market Domination does not change Google's results or ads and does not guarantee rankings. For a business that mainly needs to rank higher on Google itself, Eye To Ad Media says it will recommend SEO work first.

Availability

Slot availability for any industry and state can be checked on the Total Market Domination page or by phone at 1-800-481-8638.

About Eye To Ad Media

Founded in 2012, Eye To Ad Media is an agency at 1001 Bannock St #660 in Denver. It runs search engine optimization, AI search visibility, website and advertising programs for small and mid-sized businesses, and it operates the USABusinessSearch.com and COBusinessList.com directories as well as Distribute Press Releases.

items.title: Elevation Health Lays Out Three Care Paths for Metabolic Health, With Online Access Around the Clock
items.summary: Denver telehealth provider Elevation Health names its three care paths and explains how licensed providers handle prescriptions. Online 24/7.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 11, 2026 — Elevation Health, a Denver-based online telehealth provider, has set out the three care paths it offers people working on their metabolic health: Essential Peptide Care, Personalized Strategy, and The 90-Day Optimization Experience. Its services are available online 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so people can start the process from home on their own schedule.

The company's model combines prescription GLP-1 therapy and peptide-based metabolic care with oversight from registered dietitians, and prescriptions are filled through licensed pharmacy partners. Prescription eligibility is determined by a licensed provider. Not everyone who applies will be a candidate for medication, and Elevation Health does not promise any particular result.

Three ways to start

  • Essential Peptide Care
  • Personalized Strategy
  • The 90-Day Optimization Experience

Elevation Health says it names the three paths openly because people arrive at different starting points. Some want to understand their options before committing to anything. Others are ready for a longer, structured program. Seeing the choices side by side lets a person ask about the level of support that fits instead of guessing what is on offer, and the details of each path are on the company's website.

Metabolic health isn't one-size-fits-all, and a prescription on its own isn't a plan. Our founders are registered dietitians, and we built these three paths so people can choose the depth of support they actually want, with a licensed provider deciding what is medically appropriate.

Elevation Health, in a company statement.

How prescriptions are handled

Any medication is prescribed only after a licensed provider reviews a person's health history and decides it is appropriate. Medications are filled through licensed pharmacy partners rather than by Elevation Health directly. Registered-dietitian oversight is part of the model, so nutrition and habits are addressed alongside any prescription.

Easier to find

Elevation Health now has a free business listing on COBusinessList.com, the Colorado business directory, published on Oct. 1, 2026, under Wellness and alternative health. It also has a business page on allofus.one, a free social platform built in Denver, where people can find the company and its links in one place.

Availability

Information about all three care paths is available at elevationhealth.co and loseweightonglp1.com. Questions can be sent to the company by email.

This announcement describes services and a process, not medical advice. Only a licensed provider who has reviewed someone's history can decide if a medication suits them.

About Elevation Health

Elevation Health is an online telehealth provider based in Denver, Colorado, founded by two registered dietitians. It offers prescription GLP-1 therapy and peptide-based metabolic care with registered-dietitian oversight, filled through licensed pharmacy partners, across three programs: Essential Peptide Care, Personalized Strategy, and The 90-Day Optimization Experience. Learn more at elevationhealth.co.

items.title: allofus.one Opens Its Free Social Platform in Beta: One Account for a Chronological Feed, 3D Worlds and VR in the Browser
items.summary: allofus.one opens its free beta: one account for a chronological feed, a 3D world in the browser and VR on Quest, plus free tools.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 11, 2026 — allofus.one, a free social platform built in Denver, is now open to the public in beta at allofus.one. One account works three ways. There is a regular social feed. There is a 3D world that runs in a phone or laptop browser. And the same world opens in virtual reality on a Meta Quest headset through the headset’s web browser, with nothing to install.

The feed is chronological. Posts from the people and groups a member chooses appear in the order they were made, with no ranking algorithm deciding what to show first. Members can download their data or delete their account from the Control panel at any time. Sponsored posts in the feed are labeled, and members can switch them off in their ad settings.

One account, three ways in

  • Feed. Personal pages, connections, groups, reactions, comments, photo and video posts, polls and buy, sell and trade groups, at allofus.one.
  • 3D. A browser-based world at allofus.one/world/ with avatars, homes members can claim and build, live rooms, games and places to explore.
  • VR. The same world in WebXR on a Quest 3 headset, with controller movement, teleport, a laser pointer and a wrist menu.

Members switch between the three with the Feed, 3D and VR switcher at the top of the site, so a conversation that starts in the feed can move into the 3D world without a new sign-up.

“Your feed should show the people you chose, in the order they posted. We built that first, and then built a place to actually meet, on a phone, a laptop or a headset, with one account. It’s a beta, so we read every bug report and we want people to tell us what to fix,” allofus.one said in a statement.

Free tools built in

Every member gets the same set of free tools:

  • LIFEboard, a private planner with goals, habits, a journal, a focus timer, reminders that export to a phone calendar, and budgeting and debt-payoff calculators
  • Groups and Spaces, which give any group its own feed, members, events and courses, open or invite-only
  • Events with RSVPs, calendar files and a free video room for each event
  • Courses with ordered lessons, video links and a progress bar
  • Direct messages and video calls for up to six people in the browser, with no download and no account needed for guests
  • Brand pages, so a small business can run a page from a personal profile

Who it is for

allofus.one is aimed at people looking for an alternative to the big social networks who want to see what their friends post, along with community groups, clubs, coaches and small businesses that need events, courses and video calls without paying for separate software. Accounts are open to anyone 13 and older. The platform runs a language filter, report and block tools, and its voice chat keeps teens with teens and adults with adults.

Join the beta

The beta is free and open now. Sign up at https://allofus.one, or open allofus.one/world/ in the browser on a Quest headset to try the VR mode. Bug reports can be sent from the report button in the feed or from inside VR.

About allofus.one

allofus.one is a free social platform built in Denver. One account gives members a chronological feed, a 3D world in the browser and a VR mode for Quest headsets, plus free built-in tools including LIFEboard, groups, events, courses, direct messages and video calls. allofus.one is operated by Eye To Ad Media, headquartered in Denver, Colorado.

items.title: Aging Safely Baths Confirms Ella’s Bubbles Dealership, Putting Four Walk-In Tub Brands Under One BBB-Accredited Roof
items.summary: Aging Safely Baths is an Ella's Bubbles dealer, so families can compare Ella's Bubbles, Hydro Dimensions, Bestbath and Meditub tubs with one BBB-accredited company.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 11, 2026 — Aging Safely Baths has confirmed that it is a dealer for Ella's Bubbles walk-in tubs. With Ella's Bubbles in the lineup, the Denver-area company now offers four walk-in tub and accessible bathing brands: Hydro Dimensions, Ella's Bubbles, Bestbath (including the RANE by Bestbath line) and Meditub. A family can line up all four with one BBB-accredited company instead of booking a separate sales visit for each brand.

The confirmation targets a familiar frustration. A household that wants to compare walk-in tubs often finds that each brand is sold by a different dealer, and every dealer recommends the brand it carries. That leaves the comparison to an adult child on a laptop or a parent with a stack of brochures. Carrying several brands lets one consultation answer the practical questions side by side: which door direction fits the room, how high the seat sits, how the tub will be heated and filled, and what the existing water heater can support.

Nobody should have to pick a brand before they know what fits the bathroom. When we can show four brands in one conversation, the decision starts with the person who will use the tub and the room it has to fit, not with whoever happened to knock first.

Aging Safely Baths, in a company statement.

Questions worth asking any dealer

Aging Safely Baths suggests households bring the same short list to every quote, whoever they buy from:

  • Which brands does the dealer carry, and why does it recommend this one for this room?
  • Does the door swing inward or outward, and will it clear the toilet, vanity and doorway?
  • What is the seat height, and can the person using it sit and stand without help?
  • How is the tub heated, and does the current water heater have the capacity to fill it?
  • Who handles installation, and what does the quote include and leave out?

The company says it would rather a family walk away with clear answers than feel rushed. Its planning guides for showers sit on sister sites: roll-in-showers.com explains the 2010 ADA Standards for roll-in showers (Section 608), and bestshowerkit.com has a step-by-step worksheet for measuring a shower space.

Accredited, and easy to check

Aging Safely Baths is accredited by the Better Business Bureau, where its profile is listed as Aging Safely Walk in Tubs in Denver. The company encourages shoppers to read that profile before any in-home visit, whoever they end up hiring.

Availability

Households can ask about Ella's Bubbles or any of the other three brands by calling 1-888-779-2284 or through the contact page at agingsafelybaths.com.

About Aging Safely Baths

Aging Safely Baths is a Denver-area company that helps older adults and their families choose walk-in tubs and accessible showers so they can keep bathing safely at home. It carries Hydro Dimensions, Ella's Bubbles, Bestbath (including RANE by Bestbath) and Meditub, and it is BBB Accredited. Learn more at agingsafelybaths.com.

items.title: Eye To Ad Media Opens a Press Release Network That Routes Each Release to the Local Sites It Fits
items.summary: Every release is now republished on a news site and routed by a public filter to the Colorado and Hawaii sites it fits, with a receipt.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Distribute Press Releases, the press release service operated by Denver-based Eye To Ad Media, now sends every release it publishes through a routing network. Each release is republished on the news site Action Global News with a canonical link back to the original. A filter then reads the release's industry, location and wording and places it on up to three sites where it fits. The network launches with five sites covering Colorado camping, Denver restaurants, Denver things to do, Colorado community news and Hawaii hotels.

The filter's rules are public. A Denver restaurant opening goes to the Denver restaurant site, a camping gear launch goes to the camping site, and a Honolulu hotel announcement goes to the Hawaii site. Local sites only take local releases. Every placement keeps the original's paid or affiliated label, and every release gets a public receipt listing where it went, with a working link for each destination.

Most small companies pay for a press release and never find out where it went. We built this so every release lands somewhere it belongs, and the receipt shows you exactly where. If a release doesn't fit a site, it doesn't go there.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Eye To Ad Media.

What a release includes

Each release is published at a permanent address with news structured data, a markdown copy, a claims file and narrated audio when available. It appears in RSS, Atom, JSON Feed and Media RSS feeds filtered by industry and region, and in a company newsroom with an embed for the company's own website. New pages are submitted to IndexNow-participating search engines once they are live. The service does not promise placement on outlets it does not control and does not sell followed links. Links in every release are marked sponsored.

A single release is $99 and includes writing and one editorial pass. Monthly, annual and agency plans are listed at distributepressreleases.com/pricing. A free release builder at distributepressreleases.com/tools/release-builder shows where a draft would be routed before it is sent.

About Eye To Ad Media

Eye To Ad Media is a Denver marketing and web development firm founded in 2012. It operates Distribute Press Releases and a portfolio of local information sites, and builds websites, search programs and custom software for small and mid-sized businesses.

items.title: Eye To Ad Media Begins Custom-Coding AI Agents for Small Businesses, Starting With Lead Response
items.summary: Denver-based Eye To Ad Media now custom-codes AI agents for small businesses, starting with lead response, with a person approving every action.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Eye To Ad Media, the Denver marketing firm founded in 2012, now custom-codes AI agents for small businesses. The first builds cover three jobs: answering new inquiries within minutes, running sales-trained assistants on company websites, and handling research and content workflows. Every build is restricted to information the business has approved, and a person signs off before anything reaches a customer.

Off-the-shelf agents have become cheap or free this year, and the firm says that is the reason for the narrow focus. General-purpose tools work well when a business runs on mainstream software. The time a small company actually loses tends to sit between its own systems: a field-service CRM, a scheduling tool, a phone line and a spreadsheet that do not talk to each other. A custom agent is built to work in those gaps.

The free agents are good at common work on popular platforms. Most of the small businesses we talk to lose their time somewhere else, in the handoff between a form, a phone and a calendar. That handoff is what we build for, and nothing goes out without a person approving it.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Eye To Ad Media.

How the builds work

Each project starts with one well-defined task rather than a broad automation plan. The agent gets the narrowest permissions that do the job, read access by default, and answers only from the business's own approved material. It hands off to a person when a question falls outside that material. It keeps a log of what it did and when, and it tells customers plainly that they are talking to an automated assistant.

Lead response is the usual starting point. For local service companies, the first business to answer a new inquiry often wins the job. An agent that replies quickly, asks the qualifying questions the owner would ask and offers appointment times can make that happen at night and on weekends.

Availability

Custom agent projects are scoped individually, and cost depends on how many systems an agent touches and how much testing the workflow needs. Details and a working example are at eyetoad.com, or call 1-800-481-8638.

About Eye To Ad Media

Eye To Ad Media is a Denver marketing and web development firm founded in 2012. It builds websites, runs search and AI visibility programs, and develops custom software for small and mid-sized businesses. The company is based at 1001 Bannock St, Denver, and also operates Distribute Press Releases.

items.title: Aging Safely Baths Publishes a Six-Point Fit Check for Families Shopping for a Walk-In Tub
items.summary: Six measurements to take before requesting a walk-in tub quote, from doorway width to water heater capacity, published by the accessible bathing supplier.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Aging Safely Baths, a walk-in tub and barrier-free shower supplier operating since 2012, has published a six-point fit check for families shopping for a walk-in tub. The check covers the measurements and household details that decide whether a model will work. The company says most quote requests stall because one of them comes up after a model has been chosen.

The fit check is aimed at the adult children and spouses who usually do the research. In the company's experience, they often start from a product photo rather than the bathroom.

People fall in love with a tub online and then find out it won't go through the bathroom door. Ten minutes with a tape measure saves weeks. Measure first, then shop.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Aging Safely Baths.

The six-point fit check

1. The alcove. Measure the length, width and height of the space the current tub occupies. Many walk-in tubs are sized for a standard alcove, which can let the existing plumbing stay where it is.

2. The path in. Measure every doorway and hallway turn between the front door and the bathroom. The tub has to travel that route in one piece.

3. Door swing. Inward-opening doors suit some layouts and mobility situations, and outward-opening doors suit others. Note which way a door could open without hitting the toilet or vanity.

4. Seat height. Measure the height of a chair the bather gets out of comfortably. Seat height and depth vary between models and decide how easy the tub is to use.

5. Water heater capacity. A walk-in tub holds more water than a standard tub. Note the size and age of the water heater so it can keep up.

6. The floor. A filled tub is heavy. In older homes, or where the bathroom sits over a crawlspace, the floor is worth assessing before installation.

Availability

Aging Safely Baths supplies Bestbath and ANZZI walk-in tubs and the Bestbath line of barrier-free showers. Fit questions and quotes go through agingsafelybaths.com or 1-800-481-8638.

This is general product guidance, not medical advice. Whether a walk-in tub or hydrotherapy features suit a particular person is a question for their clinician or occupational therapist.

About Aging Safely Baths

Aging Safely Baths has supplied and installed walk-in tubs, barrier-free showers and accessible bathing products since 2012. It is an authorized Bestbath dealer and also carries ANZZI walk-in tubs. The company is based in Denver and serves households nationwide.

items.title: Aging Safely Baths Explains Curbed vs. Barrier-Free Showers for Households Replacing a Bathtub
items.summary: When a low curb is enough and when a true zero-threshold shower is worth the floor work, from a Bestbath dealer that has installed both since 2012.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Aging Safely Baths, an authorized Bestbath dealer that has supplied accessible bathing products since 2012, has published guidance for households replacing a bathtub with a shower. The guidance covers the choice between a low-curb shower and a true barrier-free, zero-threshold shower. It explains what each requires underneath the floor and who each one suits.

Replacing a tub with a shower is one of the most common accessibility projects in the home. The company says the decision is often made on looks, when the deciding factors are how the person bathing gets in and what the floor will allow.

A low curb is fine for someone who walks in steadily. A wheelchair or a rolling shower chair needs no curb at all, and that is a floor question before it is a product question. Find out what your floor will let you do, then pick the shower.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Aging Safely Baths.

When a low curb works

A curbed shower with a low threshold suits people who walk on their own or with a cane, especially with a grab bar at the entry. It usually installs without structural work. It can often go into the footprint the old tub occupied, which keeps cost and disruption down.

When to go barrier-free

A barrier-free shower suits anyone using a wheelchair, a walker or a rolling shower chair, or anyone whose mobility is expected to change. It removes the step entirely. It also brings the most structural work:

  • The pan has to sit at or below the floor. That is what makes the entry truly level.
  • Wood-framed floors usually need the subfloor modified to recess the pan.
  • Slab-on-grade floors can require cutting the slab.
  • Water containment shifts from the curb to the floor slope and the drain, so the layout matters more.

What to plan at the same time

Whichever shower is chosen, the company advises installing wall blocking for grab bars while the walls are open. It also recommends a fold-down seat or room for a shower chair and controls reachable from a seated position. Those choices cost little during the project and a great deal afterward.

Availability

Aging Safely Baths supplies the Bestbath range, including barrier-free and curbed showers, shower pans, Crestline wall systems, tub-shower combinations and walk-in tubs. Quotes are available at agingsafelybaths.com or 1-800-481-8638.

This is general product and construction guidance, not medical advice or a specification for any particular installation.

About Aging Safely Baths

Aging Safely Baths has supplied and installed walk-in tubs, barrier-free showers and accessible bathing products since 2012. It is an authorized Bestbath dealer and also carries ANZZI walk-in tubs. The company is based in Denver and serves households nationwide.
